subject: Post-call recap + technical snapshot: Aperture discovery
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Chowdhury <samir@aperture.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 02 Jun 2027 14:03:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap + technical snapshot: Aperture discovery

Samir — thanks for a productive discussion earlier. Quick written recap so we have alignment and clear next steps. I focused the notes on the technical constraints you emphasized during the call.

Top-level goals you shared
- Real-time policy classification for customer content (moderation + routing) with <300ms P95 across the end-to-end path.
- Supporting peak inference bursts around 1.5–2k requests/sec for short payloads (avg 120 tokens).
- Strong deterministic behavior and reproducibility for audit/regulatory reviews.

Primary pain points
- Current provider has high tail latency during peak business hours and opaque batching behavior.
- Cost unpredictability during bursts; procurement needs a clearer capacity/committed spend model.
- Data governance: must run in a VPC with KMS integration for keys and strict retention controls.

Initial technical snapshot (what we discussed)
- Target SLOs: 250–300ms P95 observed at the application edge (post-network), 40ms P50 for model-only token generation on short prompts.
- Throughput: design for sustained 1.5k RPS; test scaling to 2k RPS with graceful degradation via multi-tier routing.
- Models: preference for instruction-tuned open models in the 30B–70B parameter range (you mentioned open-source licensing is required). Quantization (4-bit) acceptable if we validate quality on your eval set.
- Topology options we covered: Hosted Redwood API (fastest start), Dedicated capacity (reserved GPU pool for predictable throughput), Private VPC deployment (for full network/data control). We flagged Dedicated or Private as likely for Aperture given KMS/VPC needs.

Immediate asks from Aperture for a scoped PoC
1) Share a small sample of production-like payloads (anonymized) + an eval rubric (precision/recall targets for the classifier).
2) Confirm desired SLOs for both latency and availability during business hours vs background processing.
3) Procurement contacts and any required security questionnaires (SOC2 evidence, encryption at rest/in-transit).

Recommended next steps (owner in parens)
- Redwood to send a draft Mutual Action Plan and SLA matrix (me / Marissa) — attachment: redwood-sla-matrix.pdf, aperture-mpa-draft.xlsx.
- Aperture to provide sample payloads and rubric (Samir).
- Schedule a short ops deep-dive with your infra team to validate VPC peering and KMS options (Ben to coordinate).

Timing: propose a 4-week PoC window after paperwork + sample data availability. If that works, we can scope exact metrics and success criteria in the MAP.

I’m copying Marissa (SE) for model-quality and benchmark planning and Ben (AE) for procurement and capacity modeling.

Thanks — available for a quick sync tomorrow afternoon if useful.

—
Soojin Lee
Sr. Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
soojin_lee@redwood.ai
(Attachment stubs: redwood-sla-matrix.pdf, aperture-mpa-draft.xlsx)

From: Samir Chowdhury <samir@aperture.ai>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, procurement@aperture.ai
Date: Wed, 02 Jun 2027 16:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap + technical snapshot: Aperture discovery

Thanks Soojin — this summary matches our internal notes. A few clarifications so we scope the PoC correctly: 

1) P95 target — our initial ask is 300ms P95 end-to-end for the policy classifier under 1.5k RPS sustained. We can accept up to 350ms P95 during 5–10 minute bursts while the fallback tier scales.
2) Model family — we prefer FLORA-33B (instruction-tuned variant) if Redwood can host a quantized variant with minimal quality delta. If not, FLORA-70B is our fallback if latency can be maintained.
3) Data/sample payloads — procurement will send an NDA tonight; once execs sign, I’ll share a redacted batch of ~10k samples and the rubric.

Action items from our side: procurement contact (procurement@aperture.ai) will coordinate legal; infra lead (neutralops@aperture.ai) to join the ops deep-dive.

Also quick question: for Dedicated capacity, do you support pre-warming KV caches with a prefix set and what’s the typical time to reach steady-state latency after a cold start? That will affect our ramp plan.

Appreciate the quick turnaround — Samir

From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Chowdhury <samir@aperture.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, neutralops@aperture.ai, procurement@aperture.ai
Date: Thu, 03 Jun 2027 09:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap + technical snapshot: Aperture discovery

Samir — great, thanks for the quick clarifications. Short answers and next steps below.

On Dedicated capacity pre-warm / KV cache: yes, we support explicit pre-warming. Typical path to steady-state (for short prompts and stable request distribution) is ~10–15 minutes after the pre-warm job completes; we’ll provide a pre-warm script as part of the PoC. For cold starts where no pre-warm happens, plan for a temporary tail increase for the first 30–60 minutes depending on model size and shard topology.

Model support: Marissa will run a bench comparison on FLORA-33B quantized (4-bit) vs FLORA-70B float32 to validate quality/lantency tradeoffs. If quantized FLORA-33B meets your rubric, it’s likely the most cost-effective path.

Immediate logistics
- I’ve attached a draft SLA matrix and MPA to this thread (redwood-sla-matrix.pdf, aperture-mpa-draft.xlsx). Please confirm receipt once NDA/procurement unlocks the samples.
- Ben will send a Dedicated capacity cost sketch and an ops call invite for next Tue (Ben).

Proposed timeline (condensed)
- Day 0–3: Legal/NDA + sign MAP
- Week 1: Data ingest (anonymized samples) + bench run on two model configs
- Week 2: PoC run at 200–500 RPS to validate functional correctness and metrics collection
- Week 3: Scale run to 1.5k RPS and measure P95/P50 steady-state and tail behavior

Please reply with preferred times for the ops deep-dive; Ben will propose a calendar invite for Tue/Wed next week.

Thanks — looking forward to running this together.

—
Soojin Lee
Sr. Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
soojin_lee@redwood.ai
